author: NorthEast News Desk
body: At least one person was confirmed dead and more than 30 remained missing Sunday after an inter-island ferry sank off Vanuatu, Prime Minister Jotham Napat’s office said. Search-and-rescue operations were continuing in the Pacific nation as authorities worked to account for the passengers and crew aboard the MV Matui.

The prime minister’s office said 15 people had been found alive. The vessel went down in bad weather Friday while traveling between the islands of Ambae and Santo, according to New Zealand public broadcaster RNZ. Officials had not yet released a complete passenger manifest or a definitive total for everyone aboard.

The continuing operation leaves the toll provisional. Teams face the challenge of searching open water around an island chain spread across a large area of the southwest Pacific. Authorities were expected to provide further information as survivors were located and identities confirmed. The cause of the sinking had not been established in the initial official account.
dek: Search teams continued looking for passengers and crew from the MV Matui after the inter-island vessel went down in bad weather.
headline: One dead and more than 30 missing after Vanuatu ferry sinks
location: Waters between Ambae and Santo, Vanuatu
